issues.competing_evidence: O’Donoghue+03 proposes weak transfer/hibernating-CV interpretation; Matranga+12 detects narrow X-ray eclipses and fits (1.694±0.046)×10^-13 M_sun/yr in 2006; Parsons+11/+16 favor detached/pre-CV with donor at 96–97% Roche fill; Drake+14 estimates ~10^-16 M_sun/yr from 1999 HST photospheric metals and diffusion.
issues.why_it_matters: Materially affects whether QS Vir is labeled detached/pre-CV, hibernating CV, or low-rate accretor and whether radio emission is connected to mass transfer.
issues.needed_action: Keep class/state values epoch- and method-specific. Please decide whether the community catalog should use a broad PCEB/pre-CV primary label with CV-accretion evidence as a secondary flag, or another explicit scheme; do not merge the published accretion rates.

issues.competing_evidence: Parsons+16 infers ~100 kG (~0.1 MG) weak WD field from Mg II 4481 Å line broadening and favors that over rapid rotation; the same broadening if rotational implies Pspin~700 s. Parsons+11 says Mg II indicates the WD is not rapidly rotating; Matranga+12 places a conservative B<1 MG limit from Balmer core widths/no Zeeman or cyclotron features.
issues.why_it_matters: Confusing a tentative photospheric field, a conditional spin estimate, or an upper limit with a direct field/spin measurement would bias the magnetic-CV versus weak-field comparison.
issues.needed_action: Do not adopt a measured spin or field. If a preferred display value is required, decide whether to show ~0.1 MG as tentative inference alongside <1 MG limit or leave only the upper limit. Spectropolarimetry around Mg II is needed to discriminate.

issues.competing_evidence: Qian+10 proposed a ~7.86 yr circumbinary planet; Parsons+10b found a large ~250 s timing deviation, rejected Qian’s solution, and fit an approximate ~14 yr eccentric body; Horner+13 found proposed configurations dynamically unstable (<1000 yr); Pulley+25 reports new minima invalidate the recent models and publishes a quadratic ephemeris with coefficient −8.6(6)×10^-13 d cycle^-2.
issues.why_it_matters: A fitted quadratic term, a physical Pdot, and a circumbinary companion are different claims; conflation creates a false evolutionary/planetary inference.
issues.needed_action: Retain the ephemeris coefficient as an empirical fit only; do not publish a physical Pdot or companion without a justified model and updated timing analysis. Confirm any future interpretation against new eclipse timings.

issues.competing_evidence: Ridder+25 §2.1 states VLA observations on 2022-11-28, 2022-12-28, 2023-01-09, while Tables 2–4 label the middle epoch 2022-12-22. Corrigendum corrects spectral-index signs but does not address this mismatch.
issues.why_it_matters: The date sets radio observation state/phase and the relationship to Swift observations on 2022-12-31.
issues.needed_action: Check the VLA project archive (22B-257) or authors’ data/products to establish the middle epoch’s true date; until then retain the table’s 2022-12-22 label and flag the prose conflict.

issues.competing_evidence: Rawdog inherited 8.5±0.9×10^-13 erg cm^-2 s^-1 at 1–10 keV with Webb+20 as sole citation. Ridder+23 Table 4 is the source of the converted comparison flux; §3.2 says 4XMM-DR11 full-band minus Bands 1–2 and that errors are floored at 10%. The value is not a source-specific spectral fit or contemporaneous with radio.
issues.why_it_matters: Mislabeling a catalogue-based approximate conversion as a direct XMM spectral measurement or simultaneous radio/X-ray datum can bias radio/X-ray luminosity comparisons.
issues.needed_action: Keep Webb+20 as catalogue paper and Ridder+23 as conversion/source table; preserve the 10% error floor, band convention, and epoch/state limitation. Do not calculate a simultaneous radio/X-ray ratio from it.
